s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful lower-extremity swelling and erythema with systemic symptoms and atypical mononuclear cell infiltrate
salient_findings: Painful left lower-extremity swelling and erythema
Intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, decreased appetite, and palpitations
Ill-defined, warm, confluent erythema, edema, and tender induration on the left calf
Gastrocnemius myositis, extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema, and popliteal lymphadenopathy
key_facts: Bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses noted six months earlier
Denies trauma or injury to the leg
CT and MRI of the leg revealed gastrocnemius myositis and extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema
Punch biopsy of skin from the lower leg showed a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells
No improvement with intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Atypical mononuclear cell infiltrate and subcutaneous involvement

shortlist.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and atypical mononuclear cell infiltrate

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms and atypical lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous and skin involvement with atypical lymphoid cells

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lower-extremity swelling, erythema, and myositis, along with the biopsy findings of a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, is consistent with subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, which is a rare subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that primarily affects the subcutaneous tissue.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the lack of nasal or upper respiratory tract involvement and the absence of typical immunophenotypic markers for natural killer/T-cell lymphoma in the biopsy findings.

rejected.label: Cytophagic histiocytic panniculitis
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar skin and subcutaneous findings, it is typically associated with systemic histiocytosis and hemophagocytosis, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the lack of systemic symptoms such as fever, night sweats, and weight loss, and the absence of typical lymph node involvement and immunophenotypic markers for angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the lack of typical cutaneous lesions and the absence of immunophenotypic markers for gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma in the biopsy findings.
